newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds to remain bearish below 107-25.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds to remain bearish below 107-25.

text.p: June T-bonds will remain bearish while they remain below 107-25 and they may slide towards 106-20 on Friday, technical analysts said.
Philippe Cahen, technical analyst at Credit Lyonnais in Paris, said that level would cap the market for this session.
"The market should decline further," he said.
"Resistance is the hourly Bollinger moving average at 107-25, and while we stay below that level the market is bearish."
Bollinger bands are lines drawn at standard deviations around the price action to give support and resistance.
At 1016 GMT, June T-bond futures were at 107-06 in automated trade, down four ticks from Thursday's Chicago settlement.
Cahen predicted a decline from hourly charts.
"The upper Bollinger band is going up, the lower band is going down and so is the parabloic, and stochastics and MACD are not oversold," he said.
He added that daily stochastics and MACD studies also pointed to a move lower if they were at overbought levels by the end of Friday's trading session.
He said the first target would be 106-20.

"We may go down to that level," Cahen said. "If we get there quickly then the market will not be oversold on a weekly basis and it should slip a bit more to the level of the lower Bollinger band at 105-28."
Donna Liu, technical analyst at DKB International in London, said the near term picture looked positive.
"Yesterday the turn in the moving average was unusual but so long as the market doesn't stay below 106-25 we still like it in the short term," she said.
Daily charts show that level was the low on April 1.
To the upside, she said the important resistance levels were 107-14 and 107-20.
"If the market rebounds above 107-20 it should continue to go higher," she said.
At the short end, September Eurodollars were at 93.670, down 0.020 on the day.
